playbook.intent: The agent shipped a hallucinated answer to a real user, called a tool it had no business calling, or talked itself past its own constraints — and the first instinct in the room is to find whoever wrote the prompt. It ends with the cause pinned to a single layer, a failing eval case landed before anybody touched the fix, and a write-up that names mechanisms instead of people.
playbook.scope: When the agent ships a hallucinated answer, mis-calls a tool, or jailbreaks itself, the team produces a structured postmortem that attributes cause to model/prompt/tool/context layer, lands a regression eval, and prevents recurrence.

success-criteria.criterion: The incident record carries the exact input, the trajectory it produced and the output that reached the user, so severity can be judged without asking anyone who was there
Cause is attributed to one layer — the model itself, the prompt, a tool contract, or what happened to be in context at the time — rather than left as a general misbehaviour
An eval case reproducing the failure was committed before any fix was written, and it went red against the build that was live during the incident
That same case passes after the change, and the rest of the suite did not regress to buy the pass
A human reviewed and edited the write-up before it was published, rather than letting the tooling post its own draft
The write-up names missing controls and follow-ups with owners against them, and no individual is identified as the cause
